name: DaVinci Fairlight Dialogue Ambience And Bus Mix
use_when: A Resolve scene needs professional-feeling dialogue, ambience, music, SFX, and mix control.
Audio needs more detail than the Edit page can comfortably provide.
Related SFX or dialogue tracks should be controlled together through buses.
avoid_when: The edit is silent or audio is already mixed by a dedicated sound engineer.
The project only needs a tiny volume trim and no track/bus organization.
The agent cannot check the full mix after soloing tracks.

timeline_pattern.pattern: dialogue_channel_map -> unlink_or_trim -> range_gain_or_delete -> ambience_bed -> music_fit -> obvious_sfx_pass -> tracks_groups_buses -> EQ_dynamics -> full_mix_qc
timeline_pattern.track_rule: Use separate tracks for dialogue, ambience, music, and SFX families.
timeline_pattern.range_rule: Use Range or Focus mode for partial clip edits without unnecessary splits.
timeline_pattern.ambience_rule: Add room tone or ambience under gaps so dialogue scenes do not fall into dead air.
timeline_pattern.sfx_pass_rule: Add obvious expected story sounds first, then layer secondary texture.
timeline_pattern.bus_rule: Route related tracks to buses for shared volume, EQ, reverb, or dynamics, and route buses to the main output.

motion.rule: SFX should land on visible action, impacts, object movement, or story reveals.

sound.rule: Mix by clips, tracks, and buses; speech remains clear unless the section is intentionally music-led.

keyframe_values.ambience_level: Lower ambience until it is barely noticed but prevents empty silence.
keyframe_values.music_splice: Shorten music on beats, phrase endings, or visually similar waveform peaks; crossfade when the splice is exposed.
keyframe_values.eq_distance: Reduce high frequencies to make off-screen, outside-room, or behind-door sounds feel farther away.
keyframe_values.compression: Use gentle dialogue compression with only modest gain reduction, then add makeup gain for intelligibility.

captions.rule: Captions can support hard-to-hear lines, but the mix should not bury normal dialogue.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use channelmap/pan, volume envelopes, afade/acrossfade, equalizer/lowpass, compand/dynaudnorm where appropriate, and loudness checks.
implementation.remotion: Represent tracks and buses as grouped audio components with gain envelopes, EQ/filter metadata, and routing to a main mix.
implementation.blender: Use VSE audio strips on separate tracks with volume keyframes and export loudness checks.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Separate dialogue, ambience, music, and SFX tracks; use fades, keyframes, EQ/noise tools, and grouped exports if available.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use track names, Audio Track Mixer/Submixes, Essential Sound, EQ, compression, clip gain, markers, and full-mix review.

common_mistakes: Leaving production WAV channels mapped so dialogue plays only on one speaker.
Mixing while soloed and never checking the full scene.
Adding SFX randomly instead of in story/action passes.
Routing tracks to a bus that does not reach the main output.
Overcompressing dialogue until it sounds crushed or noisy.
Leaving dead air where room tone or ambience should support the scene.
qc: Is dialogue mapped correctly and audible in the intended speakers?
Are dialogue, ambience, music, and SFX controllable on separate tracks or buses?
Does ambience prevent empty-feeling dead air without drawing attention?
Do SFX land on visible story actions and remain balanced in the full mix?
Do buses route to the main output and avoid clipping?
Does dialogue compression improve clarity without sounding artificial?
